original_question: For finite-dimensional irreducible modules of A_q, q-analogs of Davies' relations are described as polynomial relations of total degree 2N+1 in W_0 and W_1 that vanish on the module, and A_q^{[2N+1]} is defined to be the quotient of A_q by these relations. When N=1 this quotient is isomorphic to the Askey-Wilson algebra AW(3), and there is a known homomorphism from AW(3) to the double affine Hecke algebra of type C_1,C_1^∨. Is there a homomorphism from A_q^{[2N+1]} to an algebra that generalizes the double affine Hecke algebra of type C_1,C_1^∨?
target_in_paper: Problem 2-a: "Is there an homomorphism from A_q^{[2N+1]} to an algebra that generalizes the double affine Hecke algebra of C_1, C_1^∨?" This is stated immediately after the paragraph defining A_q^{[2N+1]} from q-analogues of Davies' relations for finite-dimensional irreducible modules of A_q^{diag}. ([ems.press](https://ems.press/content/serial-article-files/46556))
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the paper's second open problem, including the role of the quotient A_q^{[2N+1]}, the special case N = 1 giving the Askey-Wilson algebra AW(3), and the motivating comparison with the known homomorphism from AW(3) to the double affine Hecke algebra of type C_1, C_1^∨. ([ems.press](https://ems.press/content/serial-article-files/46556))
missing_details: The paper does not take the quotient of A_q here; it takes the quotient of A_q^{diag}. Likewise, the relevant finite-dimensional irreducible modules are modules of A_q^{diag}, not of A_q. ([ems.press](https://ems.press/content/serial-article-files/46556))

A_q^{diag} is introduced as a current algebra obtained from a certain quotient of the reflection equation algebra, and Problem 2-a is asked in that augmented q-Onsager/current-algebra setting. ([ems.press](https://ems.press/content/serial-article-files/46556))

The paper only specifies the defining extra relations schematically: they are 'certain polynomials of total degree 2N + 1 in W_0, W_1' that vanish on a finite-dimensional irreducible module. It does not provide a universal explicit polynomial formula in this note, so a faithful restatement should not over-specify them. ([ems.press](https://ems.press/content/serial-article-files/46556))

W_0 and W_1 should be identified as the two generators of the q-Onsager algebra introduced earlier in the note via the q-Dolan-Grady-type relations; your draft uses them but does not locate them in the paper's notation. ([ems.press](https://ems.press/content/serial-article-files/46556))
The paper assumes q is not a root of unity (footnote 1 on p. 542), but does not further pin down the ground field in Problem 2-a. ([ems.press](https://ems.press/content/serial-article-files/46556))

The paper's formulation is an existence question only: it asks whether there exists such a homomorphism, not for a full classification, uniqueness statement, or explicit construction of the target algebra. ([ems.press](https://ems.press/content/serial-article-files/46556))

No extra homogeneity hypothesis beyond 'total degree 2N + 1,' no nilpotency condition, and no qualifier such as 'for all sufficiently large m' appear in this statement; adding any of those would broaden or alter the problem. ([ems.press](https://ems.press/content/serial-article-files/46556))
refined_question: Assume q is not a root of unity. Let A_q^{diag} be the current algebra obtained from a certain quotient of the reflection equation algebra, and let A_q^{[2N+1]} denote the quotient of A_q^{diag} by the q-analogues of Davies' relations arising on finite-dimensional irreducible A_q^{diag}-modules, i.e. by relations asserting that certain polynomials in the q-Onsager generators W_0 and W_1 of total degree 2N + 1 vanish on the module. Since A_q^{[3]} is isomorphic to the Askey-Wilson algebra AW(3) when N = 1, and AW(3) admits a homomorphism to the double affine Hecke algebra of type C_1, C_1^∨, does there exist a homomorphism from A_q^{[2N+1]} to an algebra generalizing the double affine Hecke algebra of type C_1, C_1^∨? ([ems.press](https://ems.press/content/serial-article-files/46556))
justification: The draft is clearly targeting Problem 2-a rather than the earlier isomorphism problems. The decisive clues are the sequence 'q-analogues of Davies' relations' -> 'quotient A_q^{[2N+1]}' -> 'N = 1 gives AW(3)' -> 'known homomorphism from AW(3) to the DAHA of type C_1, C_1^∨,' which is exactly the setup immediately preceding Problem 2-a on p. 543. The main paper-faithful correction is that the quotient is of A_q^{diag}, not of A_q. ([ems.press](https://ems.press/content/serial-article-files/46556))
